lessons.title: Reading Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Reading Comprehension

Q. (Reading A1) In paragraph 1, ___ details of the Rasool's (SAW) characteristics are given.

(a) general   (b) specific   (c) chronological — Correct answer: general

Q. (Reading A2) The key idea of paragraph 2 is that:

(a) Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was a great orator   (b) Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was a just head of the state   (c) Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was just and fair even before his Nabuwat — Correct answer: Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was just and fair even before his Nabuwat

Q. (Reading A3) Examples given in paragraphs 3 and 4 show that:

(a) Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was a just head of the state   (b) Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was a simple man   (c) Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was fair in his dealing — Correct answer: Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was a just head of the state

Q. (Reading A4) Paragraph 5 shows that:

(a) Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was a just head of the state   (b) The justice of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was a source of peace and security for the non-Muslims   (c) Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was just and fair even before his Nabuwat — Correct answer: The justice of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was a source of peace and security for the non-Muslims

Q. (Reading A5) To whom did the Rasool (SAW) give this advice: "When two men come to you for judgment, never decide in favour of one without hearing the arguments of the other"?

(a) Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA)   (b) Hazrat Ali (RA)   (c) Hazrat Umar Farooq (RA) — Correct answer: Hazrat Ali (RA)

Q. (Reading B) What is the topic sentence of paragraph 3?

Ans. The topic sentence of paragraph 3 is: 'The high and noble character of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) as the Messenger of Allah (SAW) was, in fact, the main factor which led the Makkans to accept his judgements in all the disputes that arose among them.'

Q. (Reading C1) How can people achieve perfection in the moral, spiritual and social areas of life?

Ans. People can achieve perfection in the moral, spiritual and social areas of life by following the examples of the Rasool (SAW), whose life and deeds are a perfect model. He was the first and only example in the history of mankind of the perfection of morality, of spirituality and of successful leadership in the social, political, economic and other fields of life.

Q. (Reading C2) How did the Rasool (SAW) set high and noble ideals for all mankind?

Ans. The Rasool (SAW) set high and noble ideals for all mankind through his truth, honesty and trustworthiness. By sticking to these principles, he set standards of justice for people in all areas of life, and his high character convinced even his opponents to accept his judgements.

Q. (Reading C3) How were people of Makkah convinced of the Rasool's (SAW) justice even before his Nabuwat?

Ans. Before Nabuwat, the people of Makkah were convinced of his justice by the incident of the placing of the Black Stone (Hajr-e-Aswad) in the Kaaba. The tribes were about to fight over the honour, but all accepted his wise decision: he put the stone on a cloth, let every tribe's chief hold a corner, lifted it to its place and fixed it with his own hands.

Q. (Reading C4) What standards of justice did the Rasool (SAW) practise as head of the state of Madinah?

Ans. As head of the state of Madinah, the Rasool (SAW) established brotherhood between the Muhajirin and the Ansar, brought forty Jewish and pagan tribes together under one umbrella, and guaranteed social, political, religious and economic rights to all. He never allowed personal likes or dislikes to influence his judgements.

Q. (Reading C5) What made the non-Muslims bring their suits to the Rasool (SAW)?

Ans. The non-Muslims brought their suits to the Rasool (SAW) because they were convinced of his justice and trustworthiness. They knew he would decide purely on merit, without any discrimination between a Muslim and a non-Muslim.

Q. (Reading C6) How does the Holy Quran describe the personality of the Rasool (SAW)?

Ans. The Holy Quran describes the Rasool (SAW) as a mercy for all the worlds (Rahmat-ul-lil-Alameen) and as an excellent model (Uswa-e-Hasana) for mankind. It declares that he was sent to perfect the moral values and to guide humanity to the path of Allah.

lessons.title: Vocabulary
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

Q. (Vocabulary A) Give the meaning of each word as used in the lesson: model, piety, eternal, earned, sermon, revenge, commandment, upheld, destitute, proclaimed, transcends.

Ans. model: a perfect example to follow; piety: devotion to religion, godliness; eternal: lasting forever; earned: gained by work or merit; sermon: a religious talk or address; revenge: punishment given in return for a wrong; commandment: an order or rule given by Allah; upheld: maintained, supported; destitute: having no money or possessions, very poor; proclaimed: announced publicly; transcends: goes beyond the limits of.

Q. (Vocabulary B) Choose the appropriate synonyms: (i) equitable (ii) ancestor (iii) foe (iv) firm (v) glorious.

Ans. (i) equitable = fair; (ii) ancestor = forefather; (iii) foe = enemy; (iv) firm = persistent; (v) glorious = splendid.

Q. (Vocabulary C) Give meanings of the following phrasal verbs and use them in sentences: guilty of, belong to, exchange for, in accordance with.

Ans. guilty of: having committed a crime — The thief was found guilty of stealing. belong to: be the property of / be a member of — This book belongs to Ali. exchange for: give something and receive another in return — He exchanged his old car for a new one. in accordance with: following a rule — The case was decided in accordance with the law.

Q. (Vocabulary D) Translate paragraph 1 of the lesson into Urdu (model).

Ans. Model translation: حضرت محمد ﷺ کی زندگی ان لوگوں کے لیے کامل نمونہ اور مثال ہے جو نیکی، پرہیزگاری اور انفرادی و اجتماعی زندگی میں کامیابی حاصل کرنا چاہتے ہیں۔ لوگ آپ ﷺ کے پیغام سے روشنی اور آپ کی زندگی سے رہنمائی حاصل کر کے اخلاقی، روحانی اور معاشرتی شعبوں میں کمال حاصل کر سکتے ہیں۔ آپ ﷺ نے اپنے عملی نمونے کے ذریعے زندگی کے ہر شعبے میں تمام انسانوں کے لیے اعلیٰ اور شریفانہ اصول قائم کیے ہیں۔

lessons.title: Grammar
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar

Q. (Grammar A) Identify whether each underlined word is a concrete or an abstract noun: 1. She puts much effort into her studies as she wants to score good marks. 2. They recommended him for his justice and truthfulness. 3. Keep the balls in that basket. 4. The dishonest trader is losing the trust of his customers. 5. He did not take good care of his pet.

Ans. 1. effort — abstract noun (marks — concrete). 2. justice, truthfulness — abstract nouns. 3. balls, basket — concrete nouns. 4. trust — abstract noun (trader, customers — concrete). 5. care — abstract noun; pet — concrete noun.

Q. (Grammar B) Choose whether each sentence needs an indefinite article (a, an), a definite article (the), or no article: 1. He asked me ___ very hard question. 2. ___ question that he asked me was easy. 3. Have you seen ___ my scarf? 4. Could you please pass me ___ salt? 5. Is there ___ good restaurant around here? 6. ___ restaurant that my friend owns is very good. 7. I have several ___ good friends. 8. ___ UAE is a beautiful country. 9. I'll see you in ___ week! 10. I'm on ___ vacation until Monday.

Ans. 1. a 2. The 3. no article 4. the 5. a 6. The 7. no article 8. The 9. a 10. no article.

Q. (Grammar C) Underline the noun phrases in the following sentences: 1. This is an old-fashioned hat. 2. We discovered Fahad's plans. 3. A rolling stone gathers no moss. 4. The recent flood caused heavy damage. 5. An oral presentation can be interesting.

Ans. 1. an old-fashioned hat 2. Fahad's plans 3. A rolling stone 4. The recent flood 5. An oral presentation.

Q. (Grammar D) Fill in each blank with the past indefinite or past continuous tense of the verb in brackets: 1. What ___ (you/do) when I ___ (call) you last night? 2. I ___ (sit) in the café when you ___ (call) me. 3. When you ___ (arrive) at the bus stand, who ___ (be) there? 4. Shamsa ___ (watch) a film when she ___ (hear) the noise. 5. We ___ (play) tennis when Javed ___ (hurt) his ankle.

Ans. 1. What were you doing when I called you last night? 2. I was sitting in the café when you called me. 3. When you arrived at the bus stand, who was there? 4. Shamsa was watching a film when she heard the noise. 5. We were playing tennis when Javed hurt his ankle.

Q. (Grammar E) Punctuate the following paragraph: "during the sermon an ansari seeing some men from the tribe of banu tha'lba sitting there stood up and pointed towards them and said oh rasool of Allah their ancestors killed a member of our family we appeal to you to get one of them hanged in exchange for that the rasool replied the revenge of the father cannot be taken on his son"

Ans. During the sermon, an Ansari, seeing some men from the tribe of Banu Tha'lba sitting there, stood up and pointed towards them and said, "Oh Rasool of Allah! Their ancestors killed a member of our family. We appeal to you to get one of them hanged in exchange for that." The Rasool (SAW) replied, "The revenge of the father cannot be taken on his son."

Q. (Grammar F) Which words in the pronunciation key have the same pronunciation as the underlined sounds in: life, family, barriers, case, forgave, destitute, suits? Give the symbol of each underlined sound.

Ans. life: /aɪ/ as in "my" — same as "light". family: /æ/ as in "cat" (first syllable) and /i/ as in "happy" (last sound). barriers: /æ/ as in "cat". case: /eɪ/ as in "say". forgave: /eɪ/ as in "say". destitute: /e/ as in "ten" and /uː/ as in "too". suits: /uː/ as in "too".

mcqs.q: In the sentence 'She puts much effort into her studies', the word 'effort' is:
mcqs.why: Grammar A identifies 'effort' as an abstract noun because it names something that cannot be seen or touched; 'marks' in the same sentence is concrete.

mcqs.q: 'Justice' and 'truthfulness' in 'They recommended him for his justice and truthfulness' are:
mcqs.why: Grammar A marks justice and truthfulness as abstract nouns: they name qualities, not things that can be seen or touched.

mcqs.q: 'Balls' and 'basket' in 'Keep the balls in that basket' are:
mcqs.why: Grammar A identifies balls and basket as concrete nouns because they are physical things that can be seen and touched.

mcqs.q: Fill in the correct article: 'He asked me ___ very hard question.'
mcqs.why: Grammar B keys this as 'a': a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time takes the indefinite article, and 'very' begins with a consonant sound.

mcqs.q: Fill in the correct article: '___ UAE is a beautiful country.'
mcqs.why: Grammar B keys 'The UAE': names of unions of states take the definite article 'the', unlike most single country names.

mcqs.q: Fill in the correct article: 'Could you please pass me ___ salt?'
mcqs.why: Grammar B keys 'the salt': the salt is a specific, known item on the table, so the definite article is used.

mcqs.q: Underline the noun phrase in: 'The recent flood caused heavy damage.'
mcqs.why: Grammar C underlines 'The recent flood' as the noun phrase: the article, adjective and noun together work as the subject of the sentence.

mcqs.q: Complete with the correct tenses: 'Shamsa ___ (watch) a film when she ___ (hear) the noise.'
mcqs.why: Grammar D gives 'Shamsa was watching a film when she heard the noise': the longer action takes the past continuous and the interrupting action the past indefinite.

mcqs.q: Which is the correctly punctuated opening of the Grammar E paragraph?
options: During the sermon an Ansari seeing some men from the tribe of Banu Thalba sitting there stood up and pointed towards them and said oh Rasool of Allah
During the sermon, an Ansari, seeing some men from the tribe of Banu Tha’lba sitting there, stood up and pointed towards them and said, "Oh Rasool of Allah!"
"During the sermon, an Ansari seeing some men, from the tribe of Banu Tha’lba sitting there stood up, and pointed towards them and said Oh Rasool of Allah!"
During the sermon, an Ansari; seeing some men from the tribe of Banu Tha’lba sitting there; stood up and pointed towards them and said: Oh Rasool of Allah!
mcqs.why: Grammar E punctuates it exactly this way: commas set off the descriptive phrase, and the Ansari's spoken words are placed inside quotation marks.

mcqs.q: The underlined sound in 'case' has the same pronunciation as the key word:
mcqs.why: Grammar F gives 'case' the symbol /eɪ/, the same sound as in 'say'; 'life' has /aɪ/ as in 'my' and 'family' begins with /æ/ as in 'cat'.

lessons.title: Writing Skills
lessons.notes_html:
Writing Skills

Q. (Writing A) Write a précis of paragraph 5 of the unit (model).

Ans. Model précis: The Rasool (SAW) was so famous for his justice that even the Jews, his bitter enemies, brought their cases to him, and he decided them according to the Jewish law. He strictly obeyed Allah's command to judge with equity, for Allah loves those who judge fairly.

Q. (Writing B) Write an essay (220–250 words) on "Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) as an Exemplary Judge" (model, abridged).

Ans. Model essay (abridged): Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) is the perfect model of justice for all mankind. Even before Nabuwat, as a young trader, he was known for honest and fair dealing, and his just settlement of the Black Stone dispute saved the tribes of Makkah from bloodshed. As head of the state of Madinah, he decided every case on merit, without regard to colour, creed or race. When a Quraish woman was found guilty of stealing and intercession was made for her, he refused, saying that Bani Israil were ruined because they applied the law to the poor and forgave the rich. Non-Muslims trusted his justice and brought their suits to him. On his deathbed he offered his own person and property to anyone he might have wronged. Truly, no one could be more firm for justice than him.

mcqs.why: Writing B says that even before Nabuwat, as a young trader, he was known for honest and fair dealing, and his Black Stone settlement saved Makkah from bloodshed.

mcqs.why: Writing B quotes his reason: nations before were ruined because the law was applied to the poor while the rich were forgiven, which is discrimination in justice.

options: his own person and property to anyone he might have wronged
mcqs.why: The model essay ends with this unmatched example: on his deathbed he offered his own person and property to anyone he might have wronged.

options: Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) as an Exemplary Judge
mcqs.why: Writing B is the model essay of 220-250 words on 'Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) as an Exemplary Judge', built from the unit's justice examples.

mcqs.why: Writing B says his just settlement of the Black Stone dispute saved the tribes of Makkah from bloodshed, since every tribe wanted the honour of placing the stone.

lessons.title: Reading & Vocabulary
lessons.notes_html:
Reading Comprehension

Q. How do the Chinese prepare for the New Year celebrations?

Ans. Before the New Year, Chinese families clean their houses thoroughly to sweep away bad luck and decorate them with red lanterns, couplets and paper cuttings. They also buy new clothes and prepare special food for the family reunion dinner.

Q. Why is red colour important in Chinese New Year celebrations?

Ans. Red is the colour of good luck, happiness and prosperity in Chinese culture. People wear red clothes, give money in red envelopes and decorate their homes in red to keep away evil spirits.

Q. What is the importance of the reunion dinner?

Ans. The reunion dinner on New Year's Eve is the most important meal of the year. All family members, wherever they are, try to return home so that the whole family eats together and renews its bonds.

Vocabulary

Q. Explain the meanings of the phrases: 'sweep away' and 'reunion'.

Ans. Sweep away means to remove completely, as dirt is removed by sweeping. Reunion means the coming together of people again after a separation, especially family members.

Book MCQs

Q. Chinese New Year is also called:

(a) Moon Festival   (b) Spring Festival   (c) Dragon Festival   (d) Lantern Day — Correct answer: Spring Festival

Q. Money is given to children in:

(a) gold boxes   (b) red envelopes   (c) silk bags   (d) paper boats — Correct answer: red envelopes

True or False

True or False: Chinese families clean their houses to welcome bad luck. — False. They clean their houses to sweep away bad luck and to welcome good luck, happiness and prosperity.

True or False: The reunion dinner is an important part of Chinese New Year. — True.

lessons.title: Grammar & Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar

Q. Present indefinite tense: give the rule and two examples from the theme of the unit.

Ans. The present indefinite tense shows a habit or a general truth: subject + first form of verb (+ s/es with he, she, it). Examples: The Chinese celebrate the New Year in spring. She wears a red dress.

Q. Use of must/mustn't: explain with examples.

Ans. Must shows strong obligation: We must respect our elders. Mustn't shows prohibition: We mustn't waste food during celebrations.

Writing Skills

lessons.notes_html:
Reading Comprehension

Q. What is the theme of the poem 'Try Again'?

Ans. The theme of the poem is perseverance. The poet teaches that failure is not final; if we fail once, we should try again and again until we succeed, because success belongs to those who never give up.

Q. What should a person do when he fails in achieving his goal?

Ans. He should not lose heart or feel ashamed. He should learn from his mistakes, gather courage and try again, because every great achievement in history was won after repeated failures.

Q. How does the poet encourage the readers in the poem?

Ans. The poet encourages the readers by saying that all great men achieved success through perseverance. He asks them to keep trying patiently, because time and effort can turn failure into victory.

Vocabulary

Q. Give synonyms of: 'persevere', 'achieve' and 'defeat'.

Ans. Persevere — persist, keep trying. Achieve — accomplish, attain. Defeat (noun) — failure, loss; its antonym is victory.

Book MCQs

Q. The poet of 'Try Again' advises us to:

(a) give up after failure   (b) try again and again   (c) avoid hard work   (d) fear failure — Correct answer: try again and again

Q. A simile uses the words:

(a) and, but   (b) like, as   (c) in, on   (d) very, too — Correct answer: like, as

True or False

True or False: Failure is the final end of a person's efforts, according to the poem. — False. The poem teaches that failure is not final; a person should learn from his mistakes and try again and again until he succeeds.

True or False: Great men succeeded through perseverance. — True.

mcqs.why: The vocabulary answer gives persist and keep trying as synonyms of persevere.

mcqs.why: The vocabulary answer gives accomplish and attain as synonyms of achieve.

Grammar

Q. Simile and alliteration: define with examples.

Ans. A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as', e.g. He fought like a lion. Alliteration is the repetition of the same first sound in nearby words, e.g. 'Try, try again, till success is won.'

Q. Degrees of adjectives: give the three degrees of 'great' and 'good'.

Ans. Great — greater — greatest. Good — better — best. The positive degree names a quality, the comparative compares two, and the superlative compares more than two.

Writing Skills

Q. Write a paragraph on 'Perseverance is the Key to Success' (model).

Ans. Model paragraph: Perseverance means continuing to try despite difficulties. The history of every successful person is full of failures that were defeated by patience and hard work. A student who fails in an examination but tries again sincerely surely succeeds one day. Therefore we should never give up, because trying again is the surest key to success.

mcqs.q: What is a simile?
options: The repetition of the same first sound
A comparison of two things using like or as
The third degree of an adjective
A word that names a quality
mcqs.why: The grammar answer says a simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as', such as 'He fought like a lion.'

mcqs.q: Which sentence contains a simile from the unit?
options: Try, try again, till success is won.
Time can turn failure into victory.
mcqs.why: The grammar answer gives 'He fought like a lion' as the example of a simile using the word like.

options: A comparison using like or as
The superlative degree of an adjective
The repetition of the same first sound in nearby words
mcqs.why: The grammar answer defines alliteration as the repetition of the same first sound in nearby words.

options: It compares more than two things
It repeats the first sound of words

options: It names a quality without comparing
It compares more than two things
mcqs.why: The grammar answer says the superlative degree compares more than two things or people.

mcqs.why: The model paragraph says a student who fails but tries again sincerely surely succeeds one day.

Reading Comprehension

Q. What is first aid and why is it important?

Ans. First aid is the immediate help given to an injured or sick person before a doctor arrives. It is important because timely first aid can save a life, stop bleeding and prevent an injury from becoming worse.

Q. What things are usually kept in a first aid box?

Ans. A first aid box usually contains bandages, cotton, antiseptic lotion, scissors, adhesive tape, safety pins, ointment for burns and some basic medicines. Every home and school should keep such a box ready.

Q. How should a burn be treated as first aid?

Ans. A burn should immediately be cooled under running cold water for several minutes. Blisters should not be broken, and a clean, dry dressing should be applied before taking the patient to a doctor.

Vocabulary

Q. Give the meanings of specialized vocabulary: 'antiseptic', 'fracture' and 'bandage'.

Ans. Antiseptic is a substance that prevents infection in wounds. Fracture means a break in a bone. A bandage is a strip of cloth used to cover and protect a wound.

Book MCQs

Q. First aid is given:

(a) after hospital treatment   (b) before a doctor arrives   (c) only by doctors   (d) only in hospitals — Correct answer: before a doctor arrives

Q. A broken bone is called a:

(a) sprain   (b) fracture   (c) wound   (d) burn — Correct answer: fracture

True or False

True or False: Blisters on a burn should be broken at once. — False. Blisters should not be broken; a burn should be cooled under running cold water and covered with a clean, dry dressing.

True or False: Cold running water is used to cool a burn. — True.

lessons.notes_html:
Grammar

Q. Prefixes with 'to infinitives': explain the use of infinitive after verbs.

Ans. The 'to infinitive' (to + first form of verb) is used after many verbs to show purpose or intention: We use cold water to cool a burn. He rushed to help the injured man.

Q. Idioms with infinitives: use 'to be on the safe side' in a sentence.

Ans. Example: Take an umbrella to be on the safe side. The idiom means to act carefully in order to avoid risk.

Writing Skills

Q. Write a paragraph on 'The Importance of First Aid' (model).

Ans. Model paragraph: First aid is the first help given to a patient before medical treatment. It can save precious lives in accidents, burns and snake bites. Every school should train its students in first aid and keep a well-stocked first aid box. A little knowledge and presence of mind can prevent a minor injury from becoming a tragedy.

options: To plus the second form of the verb
To plus the first form of the verb

Reading Comprehension

Q. What does the poet hear and see in the poem 'The Rain'?

Ans. The poet hears the rich rain falling on the leaves above and the poor rain dripping on the poor leaves below. He enjoys the music of the rain and imagines the bright sun shining after the rain stops.

Q. Why does the poet call some leaves rich and others poor?

Ans. The leaves at the top receive the rain first, so the poet calls them rich. The leaves below receive only the drops that trickle down, so he calls them poor, just as rich people enjoy comforts first in society.

Q. What will happen after the rain stops?

Ans. After the rain stops, the sun will shine brightly and everything will look fresh and beautiful. The poet hopes that, like the sun after rain, happiness will follow the hardships of life.

Vocabulary

Q. Give synonyms and antonyms of: 'rich' and 'bright'.

Ans. Rich: synonym — wealthy; antonym — poor. Bright: synonym — shining; antonym — dull or dark. Such pairs are also used in the poem to create contrast.

Book MCQs

Q. The poet of 'The Rain' is:

(a) W. E. Hickson   (b) W. H. Davies   (c) John Keats   (d) William Wordsworth — Correct answer: W. H. Davies

Q. After the rain, the poet expects:

(a) a storm   (b) bright sunshine   (c) darkness   (d) flood — Correct answer: bright sunshine

True or False

True or False: The lower leaves receive the rain before the upper leaves. — False. The upper leaves receive the rain first; the lower leaves receive only the drops that trickle down from above.

True or False: The poem ends with a note of hope. — True.

mcqs.why: The solved answer says the poet hears the rich rain falling on the leaves above and enjoys the music of the rain.

mcqs.why: The solved answer says the poet hears the poor rain dripping on the poor leaves below, under the upper leaves.

mcqs.why: The vocabulary answer gives shining as the synonym of bright and dull or dark as its antonym in the solved exercise.

Grammar

Q. Metaphor and personification: define with examples from the poem.

Ans. A metaphor directly calls one thing another, e.g. the rain is called music. Personification gives human qualities to things, e.g. the sun is shown as rising and smiling after the rain.

Q. Connotation and denotation: explain briefly.

Ans. Denotation is the dictionary meaning of a word, while connotation is the feeling or idea attached to it. 'Rain' denotes falling water, but in the poem it connotes both hardship and hope.

Writing Skills

Q. Summarize the poem 'The Rain' (model summary).

Ans. Model summary: In 'The Rain', W. H. Davies describes rain falling on the upper and lower leaves of a tree. The upper leaves drink the rain first like rich people, while the lower leaves get only drops like the poor. The poet is hopeful that after the rain the sun will shine, just as joy follows sorrow in human life.

mcqs.q: What is a metaphor?
options: It directly calls one thing another
A feeling attached to a word
It gives human qualities to things
mcqs.why: The grammar answer defines a metaphor as directly calling one thing another, as when the rain is called music in the poem.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of a metaphor in the poem?
mcqs.why: The grammar answer gives this exact example: the rain is called music, so one thing is directly called another.

options: The dictionary meaning of a word
mcqs.why: The grammar answer defines personification as giving human qualities to things, as with the sun rising and smiling.

mcqs.why: The grammar answer says the sun is shown as rising and smiling after the rain, which gives it human qualities.

mcqs.q: What is denotation?
options: The feeling attached to a word
The dictionary meaning of a word
mcqs.why: The grammar answer states that denotation is the dictionary meaning of a word, unlike connotation which is the attached feeling.

mcqs.q: What is connotation?
options: The feeling or idea attached to a word
The dictionary meaning of a word
The third form of a verb
mcqs.why: The grammar answer states that connotation is the feeling or idea attached to a word, beyond its dictionary meaning.

mcqs.q: In the poem, what does the word 'rain' denote?
mcqs.why: The grammar answer says rain denotes falling water, while in the poem it connotes both hardship and hope.

mcqs.q: In the poem, what does 'rain' connote?
mcqs.why: The grammar answer says that in the poem rain connotes both hardship and hope, not merely its dictionary meaning of falling water.

Rich people, who get the rain first
mcqs.why: The model summary says the upper leaves drink the rain first like rich people, while the lower leaves get only drops like the poor.

mcqs.why: The model summary ends hopefully: after the rain the sun will shine, just as joy follows sorrow in human life.

Reading Comprehension

Q. What are the advantages of television over newspapers?

Ans. Television presents news with pictures, sound and live coverage, so events feel real and immediate. It also provides entertainment and education for the whole family, including people who cannot read.

Q. What are the advantages of newspapers over television?

Ans. Newspapers give detailed and permanent information which can be read again and again at any time. They improve reading habits and vocabulary, and they are cheap and available everywhere.

Q. Which medium does the writer finally prefer, and why?

Ans. Both media have their own importance, but newspapers develop knowledge and thinking more deeply. The writer suggests a balanced use: television for quick news and entertainment, and newspapers for serious study of events.

Vocabulary

Q. Guess the meanings of the unfamiliar words: 'broadcast' and 'circulation'.

Ans. Broadcast means to send out a programme by radio or television. Circulation means the number of copies of a newspaper sold or distributed.

Book MCQs

Q. Television presents news with:

(a) only words   (b) pictures and sound   (c) only pictures   (d) only sound — Correct answer: pictures and sound

Q. Newspapers can be:

(a) seen only once   (b) re-read many times   (c) never stored   (d) only watched — Correct answer: re-read many times

True or False

True or False: Newspapers are useless in the age of television. — False. Newspapers give detailed and permanent information, improve reading habits and vocabulary, and can be re-read at any time.

True or False: Television also serves people who cannot read. — True.

Grammar

Q. Active and passive voice: change into passive: 'The editor published the news.'

Ans. Active: The editor published the news. Passive: The news was published by the editor. Rule: object + helping verb (was/were) + third form of verb + by + subject.

Q. Transitive and intransitive verbs: explain with examples.

Ans. A transitive verb needs an object: She reads a newspaper. An intransitive verb needs no object: The baby sleeps. Many verbs can be used both ways.

Writing Skills

Q. Write a paragraph comparing television and newspapers (model).

Ans. Model paragraph: Television and newspapers are the two most popular sources of information. Television shows events live with pictures, while newspapers describe them in detail. Television entertains the whole family, but newspapers improve our reading and knowledge. In my opinion, a wise person uses both: television for quick updates and newspapers for deep understanding.

mcqs.q: What is the passive voice of 'The editor published the news'?
options: The editor was published by the news
The news was published by the editor
By the editor the news publishes
mcqs.why: The grammar answer gives this exact passive form: the news was published by the editor, following the passive voice rule.

mcqs.q: In the passive voice rule, what comes first?
options: The object of the active sentence
The subject of the active sentence
The third form of the verb
mcqs.why: The grammar rule is: object plus helping verb was or were, plus the third form of the verb, plus by, plus the subject.

mcqs.q: In the passive voice, which form of the verb is used?
mcqs.why: The grammar rule for passive voice uses the third form of the verb after the helping verb was or were, as in 'was published'.

mcqs.q: A transitive verb is a verb that:
options: Works only in the past tense
mcqs.why: The grammar answer states that a transitive verb needs an object, as in the example 'She reads a newspaper'.

mcqs.q: Which sentence has a transitive verb?
mcqs.why: The grammar answer gives this as the transitive example because the verb 'reads' takes the object 'a newspaper'.

mcqs.q: An intransitive verb is a verb that:
mcqs.why: The grammar answer states that an intransitive verb needs no object, as in the example 'The baby sleeps'.

mcqs.q: Which sentence has an intransitive verb?
mcqs.why: The grammar answer gives this as the intransitive example because the verb 'sleeps' works completely without any object.

mcqs.q: What is true about many verbs?
options: They can never take an object
They can be used both ways
mcqs.why: The grammar answer notes that many verbs can be used both ways, working both as transitive and as intransitive verbs.

mcqs.q: In the model paragraph, television shows events how?
mcqs.why: The model paragraph says television shows events live with pictures, while newspapers describe them in detail in print.

mcqs.q: In the model paragraph, a wise person uses newspapers for what?
mcqs.why: The model paragraph concludes that a wise person uses television for quick updates and newspapers for deep understanding.

Q. (Reading A1) "The last couple of years have been a long bumpy ride for me." The underlined phrase means:

(a) easy time   (b) hard and challenging time   (c) leisure time — Correct answer: hard and challenging time

Q. (Reading A2) The author thinks he will become a well-rounded student by:

(a) making good grades in academics   (b) participating in co-curricular activities   (c) partaking both in academic and co-curricular activities — Correct answer: partaking both in academic and co-curricular activities

Q. (Reading A3) His summer jobs in the preceding two years helped him:

(a) gain an understanding of independence and responsibility   (b) get financial boost   (c) make friends — Correct answer: gain an understanding of independence and responsibility

Q. (Reading A4) The author has become more ___ because of his job experiences.

(a) well-to-do and prosperous   (b) mature and responsible   (c) social and well-known — Correct answer: mature and responsible

Q. (Reading A5) This developing positive outlook has given the author the motivation he needs to become:

(a) famous   (b) wealthy   (c) successful — Correct answer: successful

Q. (Reading B1) What are some distinctions of the writer?

Ans. The writer, Jim Ryun, is a student of Washington High School who has won distinctions in studies and sports. He made the National Honour Society in his junior and senior years, is a member of the Letterman's Club and the Junior Academy of Science, and works as the editor of his school magazine 'Washington World'.

Q. (Reading B2) How has the writer spent his summer vacation?

Ans. The writer has spent his summer vacations in outdoor sports, summer jobs, school sports and contests in oratorical skills. Under the guidance of his coaches, he participated actively in these activities instead of wasting his vacation.

Q. (Reading B3) What has he gained from his summer jobs experiences?

Ans. From his summer jobs he has gained practical experience, self-confidence and financial support for his studies. The jobs taught him discipline, hard work and the value of time, and motivated him to strive for excellence.

Q. (Reading B4) How are these experiences helpful to him in future?

Ans. These experiences will help him in future because they have developed in him patience, courage, hope and the habit of working little by little towards a goal. Such training prepares a student to face the challenges of practical life successfully.

Q. (Reading B5) What kind of student is the writer? Which of his qualities impress you?

Ans. The writer is an all-round, hardworking and balanced student who excels both in studies and in co-curricular activities. The quality that impresses me most is his perseverance: he believes that 'little by little one walks far', and he never gets discouraged by failure, even in baseball, the one sport in which he did not excel.

Vocabulary

Q. (Vocabulary A) Give the meaning of each word as used in the lesson: circumstances, participant, priority, contest, preceding, excel, motivation, financially.

Ans. circumstances: the conditions or facts connected with an event; participant: a person who takes part in something; priority: the most important thing; contest: a competition in which people try to win something; preceding: coming before in time; excel: to be better than others; motivation: inspiration, the reason for doing something; financially: in money matters.

Q. (Vocabulary B) Explain each phrase as used in the lesson: (a) a long bumpy ride (b) earned the first place (c) a well-rounded student (d) along with a group of other students (e) to look forward to it (f) made it this far.

Ans. (a) a long bumpy ride: a long period full of difficulties and problems. (b) earned the first place: won the top position through hard work. (c) a well-rounded student: a student developed in all respects — studies, sports and character. (d) along with a group of other students: together with other students. (e) to look forward to it: to think about something in the future with pleasure. (f) made it this far: reached this stage or position.

Q. (Vocabulary C) Translate paragraph 1 of the lesson into Urdu (model).

Ans. Model translation: پچھلے چند سال میرے لیے ایک طویل اور دشوار گزار سفر رہے ہیں، جیسا کہ میری عمر کے ہر شخص کے لیے رہے ہیں۔ تجربات مختلف ہو سکتے ہیں لیکن ہر ایک انہی ”نوعمری“ کے حالات سے گزرا ہے جن سے میں گزرا ہوں۔ سب نے ان سے اپنے اپنے انداز میں نمٹا ہے۔

lessons.title: Grammar
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar

Q. (Grammar A) Underline the indefinite pronouns in the following sentences: 1. Everybody enjoys a good movie. 2. Does anybody have the time? 3. One sang while the other played the guitar. 4. Nobody knows the trouble I've seen. 5. The secret was known by few. 6. No, the secret was known by many. 7. Mathematics is too hard for some. 8. Surely, you recognize somebody. 9. Is there anything that I can do?

Ans. 1. Everybody 2. anybody 3. One 4. Nobody 5. few 6. many 7. some 8. somebody 9. anything.

Q. (Grammar B) Tick the verb which agrees with the indefinite pronoun: 1. Each of the family members (has, have) one vote. 2. One of the boys (eat, eats) pizza every week. 3. Both of the answers (is, are) correct. 4. A few of the staff (was, were) gone today. 5. All of the animals (run, runs) when they are scared. 6. Someone (has, have) his own thoughts. 7. You know that others (has, have) tried this.

Ans. 1. has 2. eats 3. are 4. were 5. run 6. has 7. have.

Q. (Grammar C) Fill in the blanks with the present perfect form of the verb given in brackets: 1. How long ___ (he/live) in Karachi? 2. I ___ (speak) Chinese for twenty years. 3. ___ (Aliya/fly) in an airplane before? 4. Shan ___ (not/go) to lunch yet. 5. Our class ___ (take) a field trip three times this year. 6. Where ___ (they/move) to? 7. Javeria ___ (ask) that question four times today.

Ans. 1. How long has he lived in Karachi? 2. I have spoken Chinese for twenty years. 3. Has Aliya flown in an airplane before? 4. Shan has not gone to lunch yet. 5. Our class has taken a field trip three times this year. 6. Where have they moved to? 7. Javeria has asked that question four times today.

mcqs.why: Grammar A underlines 'Everybody' as the indefinite pronoun; it refers to people in general without naming anyone in particular.

mcqs.why: Grammar A identifies 'few' as the indefinite pronoun here; in the next sentence 'many' plays the same role.

mcqs.why: Grammar B keys 'has': 'each' is singular, so it takes a singular verb even though 'members' is plural.

mcqs.why: Grammar B keys 'are': 'both' is plural, so the verb agreeing with it must also be plural.

mcqs.q: Tick the correct verb: 'A few of the staff ___ gone today.'
mcqs.why: Grammar B keys 'were': 'a few' refers to a plural number of the staff, so it takes a plural verb.

mcqs.why: Grammar B keys 'has': 'someone' is a singular indefinite pronoun and always takes a singular verb.

mcqs.why: Grammar C gives 'How long has he lived in Karachi?': the present perfect is has/have + third form of the verb (lived).

mcqs.why: Grammar C gives 'Shan has not gone to lunch yet': with 'Shan' the auxiliary is 'has' and the third form of 'go' is 'gone'.

mcqs.why: Grammar C gives 'Our class has taken a field trip three times this year': 'class' is treated as singular and 'taken' is the third form of 'take'.

mcqs.why: Grammar A underlines 'some' as the indefinite pronoun; it stands for some students without specifying who they are.

Writing Skills

Q. (Writing A) Write a précis of paragraph 2 of the unit (model).

Ans. Précis (model): The writer says that hope, patience and courage always motivated him to strive for excellence. He never felt discouraged in unfavourable circumstances and kept working little by little, believing that steady effort in accordance with a plan leads to success in every field of life.

Q. (Writing B) Write an essay (220-250 words) on 'Co-Curricular Activities — Preparing Students for Future' (model, abridged).

Ans. Model essay: Co-curricular activities are an essential part of education. Sports, debates, scouting and literary societies develop in students the qualities of leadership, teamwork, patience and courage, which books alone cannot teach. A student who takes part in these activities learns time management and gains practical experience and self-confidence. Jim Ryun's example shows that a balanced student excels in studies as well as in sports. Schools should therefore encourage every student to participate in healthy co-curricular activities, because these activities prepare students for the real challenges of future life.

Q. (Writing C) Write an application to the Principal for arranging a Sports Week in your school (model).

Ans. Model application: The Principal, Government High School, Lahore. Respected Sir, With due respect, I beg to state that the students of our school are very fond of sports, but no sports week has been arranged this year. Sports keep students healthy and develop discipline and teamwork. It is, therefore, requested that a Sports Week may kindly be arranged in our school next month. We shall be highly thankful to you. Yours obediently, X.Y.Z., Class X.

Q. (Writing D) Write to the principal of a Technology College of your district requesting information regarding admission criteria in Associate Degree of Civil Engineering (model).

Ans. Model letter: From: [Your Name], [Address], [Date]. To: The Principal, Government College of Technology, [District]. Subject: Request for information regarding admission criteria — Associate Degree of Civil Engineering. Respected Sir, I have passed my Matric (Science) examination and wish to seek admission to the Associate Degree of Civil Engineering at your college. Kindly inform me about the admission criteria, required marks, documents, last date for submission of forms and the fee structure. I shall be thankful for an early reply. Yours obediently, [Name].

Q. (Writing E) Suppose you have qualified for the award of Merit Scholarship. Fill in the application form particulars (model).

Ans. Model filled particulars: Name: (candidate's name); Father's Name: (father's name); Contact No.: (mobile number); Exam Passed: SSC, Year: (year); Roll No.: (roll number); Group: Science; Marks Obtained: (marks, copy attached); Name of Institution: (school name); Name of Present Institution: (college name); Name of Course: FSc (Pre-Medical/Pre-Engineering); Duration of Course: 2 years; Date of Admission: (date); Board/University with which the present institution is affiliated: (board name); Postal Address of the Candidate: (full address); Signature of Parent; Date; Signature of Candidate.

lessons.notes_html:
Reading Comprehension

Q. Why is peace necessary for the world?

Ans. Peace is necessary because wars destroy lives, homes and economies. Only in peace can nations develop, children study and people live without fear, so peace is the foundation of all progress.

Q. How can peace be established in the world?

Ans. Peace can be established when nations solve their disputes through dialogue instead of war. Justice, tolerance and respect for the rights of others are the true roads to lasting peace.

Q. What role can young people play in promoting peace?

Ans. Young people can promote peace by practising tolerance, avoiding violence and spreading the message of brotherhood. As future leaders, their peaceful thinking can change the destiny of the world.

Vocabulary

Q. Explain connotation and denotation with reference to the word 'peace'.

Ans. The denotation of peace is the absence of war. Its connotation is much wider: safety, harmony, justice and happiness in society.

Book MCQs

Q. Peace can be achieved through:

(a) war   (b) dialogue and justice   (c) weapons   (d) silence — Correct answer: dialogue and justice

Q. The denotation of a word is its:

(a) hidden feeling   (b) dictionary meaning   (c) opposite   (d) synonym — Correct answer: dictionary meaning

True or False

True or False: Wars are necessary for the progress of nations. — False. Wars destroy lives, homes and economies; peace is the foundation of all progress, and disputes should be solved through dialogue.

True or False: Justice is a road to lasting peace. — True.

Grammar

Q. Kinds of pronouns: name them with examples.

Ans. Personal: I, we, you, he. Possessive: my, our, his. Reflexive: myself, himself. Demonstrative: this, that. Interrogative: who, what. Relative: who, which, that.

Q. Participles: explain present and past participles with examples.

Ans. Present participle (-ing): The crying baby needs milk. Past participle (third form): The broken window was repaired. Participles work as adjectives or help in making tenses.

Writing Skills

Q. Write the main idea of the text 'Peace' (model).

Ans. Model main idea: The text teaches that peace is the greatest need of mankind. Wars bring only destruction, while peace brings progress, prosperity and happiness. Every individual and every nation must work for peace through justice, dialogue and tolerance.

mcqs.why: The grammar answer lists this and that as demonstrative pronouns, which point out the person or thing being referred to.

Reading Comprehension

Q. Why is selecting the right career important?

Ans. Selecting the right career is important because a person's whole life, happiness and success depend on it. A wrong choice leads to frustration, while the right choice makes work enjoyable and fruitful.

Q. What factors should be considered while choosing a career?

Ans. A student should consider his aptitude, interest, educational results and the demand of the market. Guidance from teachers, parents and career counsellors also helps in making a wise decision.

Q. What is the role of aptitude in career selection?

Ans. Aptitude is the natural ability for a particular work. A person succeeds quickly in the field for which he has natural aptitude, because he learns it easily and works in it with interest.

Vocabulary

Q. Explain the meanings of unfamiliar words and phrases: 'aptitude' and 'profession'.

Ans. Aptitude means natural ability or talent for something. A profession is a job that needs special education and training, such as medicine, law or teaching.

Book MCQs

Q. Career should be selected according to:

(a) friends' wishes only   (b) aptitude and interest   (c) fashion   (d) chance — Correct answer: aptitude and interest

Q. A noun clause works as a:

(a) verb   (b) noun   (c) adverb   (d) preposition — Correct answer: noun

True or False

True or False: A wrong career choice can cause lifelong frustration. — True.

True or False: Market demand has nothing to do with career selection. — False. The demand of the market is one of the factors a student should consider while choosing a career, along with aptitude and interest.

Q. Noun clause: explain with an example.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension

Reading Comprehension

Q. (Reading 1) Which areas are most affected by incessant growth in population?

Ans. Incessant population growth puts the arable land area, water, energy and biological resources under great pressure. The most affected are the people in developing countries, where nearly two billion people are living in extreme poverty, together with agriculture and food production.

Q. (Reading 2) Why are the developing countries going to suffer more due to over population?

Ans. The developing countries will suffer more because about 90 per cent of the additional people will be added there. They already face fragile economies, malnutrition, poverty and low living standards, so they cannot maintain the quality of life of their growing numbers.

Q. (Reading 3) What is the major cause of food shortages and malnutrition?

Ans. The major cause of food shortages and malnutrition is rapid population growth. The rising number of people puts great demand on the food supply system, and the food needs of the developing world will roughly double in the next fifty years.

Q. (Reading 4) How are water resources under great stress?

Ans. Water resources are under great stress because many major rivers are drying up and groundwater is being excessively used. In some areas, the groundwater is being consumed faster than it is replenished, so the water table is steadily declining.

Q. (Reading 5) What is the effect of depletion of fossil energy?

Ans. Due to the depletion of fossil energy, the energy requirement per person will be greatly reduced. Fossil energy is largely used in the fertilizer industry, so its depletion will also reduce food production.

Q. (Reading 6) What is the limitation of improved technology?

Ans. The limitation of improved technology is that, although it has increased the growth of some crops, it cannot increase food production indefinitely. There is a limit to the capacity of improved technology, and it cannot keep pace with unlimited population growth.

Q. (Reading 7) How can sufficient food supply be made possible for the future generation?

Ans. Sufficient food supply for the future generation can be made possible by limiting the growth of population and by sustaining the integrity of the ecosystem and the biological system. Only a smaller number of people can be sustained adequately by the available resources.

Q. (Reading 8) What strategies should be adopted for safe future?

Ans. For a safe future, immediate steps should be taken to limit population growth, protect arable land and water resources, use energy carefully and avoid massive use of pesticides. Sustained efforts are needed to maintain the ecosystem for the coming generations.

Grammar

Q. (Grammar A) Choose the appropriate conjunctions: 1. He couldn't go home, ___ he had no place to go. (a. but b. for c. though) 2. ___ it was hot, he was wearing a coat. (a. When b. Although c. Then) 3. I have no money, ___ I cannot go for shopping. (a. Since b. Before c. As) 4. He lost his job ___ he was often late. (a. while b. because c. or) 5. ___ I had more time, I would help you. (a. Since b. When c. If)

Ans. 1. for — He couldn't go home, for he had no place to go. 2. Although — Although it was hot, he was wearing a coat. 3. Since — Since I have no money, I cannot go for shopping. 4. because — He lost his job because he was often late. 5. If — If I had more time, I would help you.

Q. (Grammar B) Replace each adverb clause by an adverb or adverb phrase: 1. I have not been well since I returned from Murree. 2. I am glad that he has recovered from his illness. 3. As soon as I saw the cobra, I ran away. 4. He may go home after his work is finished. 5. I did not pay her, as I had no money with me.

Ans. 1. I have not been well since my return from Murree. 2. I am glad at his recovery from his illness. 3. On seeing the cobra, I ran away at once. 4. He may go home after finishing his work. 5. I did not pay her for want of money.

Q. (Grammar C) Underline the adverb clauses in the following sentences and state whether each is an adverb clause of time, place, reason, purpose, result, manner, comparison, condition or concession: 1. The frightened child ran as fast as he could. 2. Even if they hurry, they may not get there on time. 3. The player is out of the match because he has hurt himself. 4. If she recovers quickly, she will join the team. 5. The speaker was so absorbed in his speech that he forgot the time. 6. She switched on the television so that she could listen to the news. 7. They had left before the concert ended. 8. He acts as if he had owned the car. 9. Where the road bends dangerously, be more careful. 10. He will get a good job when he graduates.

Ans. 1. 'as fast as he could' — adverb clause of manner/comparison. 2. 'Even if they hurry' — condition. 3. 'because he has hurt himself' — reason. 4. 'If she recovers quickly' — condition. 5. 'that he forgot the time' — result. 6. 'so that she could listen to the news' — purpose. 7. 'before the concert ended' — time. 8. 'as if he had owned the car' — manner. 9. 'Where the road bends dangerously' — place. 10. 'when he graduates' — time.

Q. (Grammar D) Match the two clauses and make meaningful sentences: 1. The rain started 2. I had written many books 3. They had to cancel the meeting 4. You won't succeed 5. Although it was raining — (a) if you don't try hard (b) because the director did not show up (c) he went out without an umbrella (d) while I was driving home (e) before I was awarded the literature prize.

Ans. 1. The rain started while I was driving home. (1-d) 2. I had written many books before I was awarded the literature prize. (2-e) 3. They had to cancel the meeting because the director did not show up. (3-b) 4. You won't succeed if you don't try hard. (4-a) 5. Although it was raining, he went out without an umbrella. (5-c)
